paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. God cares about the regular, the daily, the on-schedule. He tells Moses to command the Israelites to present His offerings "at its appointed time" (Numbers 28:2), and then He gives a whole calendar: every morning, every twilight, every Sabbath, every new moon, every feast. Nothing on that list was random, and nothing was left for Israel to guess at.

Notice what the days have in common. Over and over, the LORD asks for animals that are "all unblemished" (Numbers 28:11), and He keeps adding a male goat as a sin offering "to make atonement for you" (Numbers 28:22). The calendar kept two things in front of Israel again and again: God is holy, and He provides a way for His people to come near. On the tenth day of the seventh month they were told, "you shall humble yourselves" (Numbers 29:7), so the rhythm was never just a checklist. It was meant to shape the heart.

So what does that mean for you, baker? A steady rhythm with God matters, even on the days that feel ordinary, because He's the One who set the times and He meets His people in them. And all those offerings point to Jesus, the Lamb who gave His life to bring people home (John 1:29). That's why my ovens stay ready, friend: I'm not guessing at the day, I'm just showing up on time, like Israel was told to.
